interactions.summary: Jiang asks the class to infer the sin from the punishment of backward-twisted heads, identifies the sinners as fortune tellers, and explains that they are punished by losing the forward sight they falsely claimed.

claims.claim: Jiang identifies the backward-looking sinners as fortune tellers who claimed to see the future and sold that claim to others.
Their punishment is ironic because they can only look backward, never ahead, after pretending to command the future.
Jiang highlights Tiresias and similar famous seers to show how much space Dante gives this category of fraud.

signature_moments.moment: Those who sold the fantasy of forward sight are condemned to a body that can only face backward.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is a vivid image of Dante's justice and becomes the anchor for Jiang's broader critique of prophetic manipulation.

chronology_notes.note: The lecture narrows fraud from institutional corruption to temporal manipulation: people who claim authority over the future.
